nodes.label: Model Merging via Task Vectors
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Task vectors = fine-tuned weights minus pretrained weights. Arithmetic operations (add, subtract, negate) on task vectors produce meaningful model behaviors. Spectral over-accumulation occurs when merging vectors with shared singular directions.

nodes.label: LoRA as Subspace Projection
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: LoRA constrains weight updates to low-rank subspace: Delta_W = BA where B in R^{d_out x r}, A in R^{r x d_in}. Factorization is non-unique (GL_r ambiguity). Singular values of B encode task-specific signal.

nodes.label: Platonic Representation Hypothesis
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Large neural networks converge to similar internal representations regardless of architecture or modality. Implies Fisher matrices and weight subspaces are approximately shared. Supports cross-architecture LoRA transfer feasibility.

nodes.label: Weight Space Learning (SymmetriesInWSL)
nodes.source_location: Paper: Symmetries in Weight Space Learning
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Algebraic proof that LoRA weight space has GL_r symmetry. Networks with the same function but different parameterizations are equivalent. Canonicalization required for learning on weights.

nodes.label: Frechet Mean in Riemannian LoRA Space
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Riemannian geometry proof that singular values of B are invariant under GL_r (Frechet mean argument). Provides metric on LoRA weight space where GL_r orbits are identified.

nodes.label: Cross-Architecture Model Comparison
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Comparing LoRA adapters trained on different architectures. TRS provides architecture-agnostic fingerprint enabling such comparison. Cross-LoRA paper provides empirical validation of cross-architecture transfer.

nodes.label: Task Identity via Spectral Analysis
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Task identity is encoded in the singular value spectrum of LoRA B matrices. Two LoRAs trained on the same task (different seeds, architectures) should have similar TRS. Empirical test: 3 models x 10 tasks x 5 seeds = 150 LoRAs.

nodes.label: LoRA Rank and Effective Rank Analysis
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Effective rank of learned LoRA B matrices often much less than nominal rank r. Effective rank relates to number of task-specific signal dimensions. sqrt(N) NTK bound provides theoretical upper limit.

nodes.label: Spectral Geometry of Task Space
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Task space has geometric structure revealed by TRS vectors. Distances in TRS space correspond to semantic task similarity. Principal angles between B-matrix column spaces measure task overlap.

edges.source_location: Paper: Symmetries in Weight Space Learning
